nodes.label: M7.2 foreshock San Felipe
nodes.description: Magnitude 7.2 shallow foreshock near San Felipe, Yaracuy, 22 km depth, 24 June 2026.

nodes.label: M7.5 mainshock Yumare
nodes.description: Magnitude 7.5 shallow mainshock near Yumare, Veroes, Yaracuy, 10 km depth, 39-40s after foreshock.

nodes.label: Extensive aftershock sequence
nodes.description: Over 1,000 aftershocks recorded by mid-July, including M5.1 Tucacas and M4.4 Guatire events, continuing to weaken structures.

nodes.label: Landslide/debris-flow risk from rains
nodes.description: Onset of rainy season, hurricanes or tropical lows could trigger landslides and mud flows on seismically weakened slopes in North Coastal Range.

nodes.label: Risk of disease outbreaks
nodes.description: PAHO identified elevated risk of measles, diphtheria, pertussis, polio, acute diarrheal disease, cholera and vector-borne illness linked to displacement and damaged WASH.

nodes.label: Deaths from earthquakes
nodes.description: Death toll rose from 32 to over 5,200 across successive reports (DFS, OCHA, UNHCR, UNFPA, UNICEF, CESVI).

nodes.label: Injuries from earthquakes
nodes.description: Injuries rose from about 700 to over 16,700 across multiple situation reports.

nodes.label: Tens of thousands missing
nodes.description: IFRC noted tens of thousands reported missing, with ambiguous unreconciled figures across sources.

nodes.label: Mass displacement/homelessness
nodes.description: Displacement estimates rose from 3,000 (OCHA) to over 17,900 homeless (UNICEF/CESVI) with people in temporary camps.

nodes.label: Collapsed/damaged buildings
nodes.description: 2,501 damaged sites including 774 housing units, 189 fully collapsed, and 38 hospitals (UNHCR); CESVI cites 856 affected buildings.

nodes.label: US$6.7-37 billion economic damage
nodes.description: UNDP preliminary estimate of $6.7bn direct physical damage; UNDRR analytical estimate of ~$37bn total direct damage to buildings and infrastructure.

nodes.label: Critical infrastructure disruption
nodes.description: Closure of Maiquetía airport, suspension of Caracas Metro/railways, power outages, damage to water, telecoms, roads and bridges.

nodes.label: Overwhelmed health system
nodes.description: Hospitals managing large trauma caseloads within an already weakened health system with pre-crisis shortages of supplies and surgical capacity.

nodes.label: Loss of livelihoods/income
nodes.description: Households lost homes, productive assets, employment; small businesses, informal commerce and tourism severely disrupted (IFRC).

nodes.label: Heightened protection risks
nodes.description: Overcrowded shelters, family separation and displacement increased GBV and protection risks especially for women, girls, disabled and older persons (UNFPA).

nodes.label: Logistics congestion at ports/airport
nodes.description: Damaged Maiquetía airport and concentration of operations at Port of La Guaira increased risk of delays in receipt, storage and distribution of supplies.

nodes.label: Unreinforced/informal construction
nodes.description: Most buildings unlikely built to modern earthquake regulations; lack of enforcement of building standards; informal settlements on unstable hillsides.

nodes.label: Protracted economic/humanitarian crisis
nodes.description: Venezuela ranked 24th/97 on INFORM Severity Index (7.6/10), nearly 8 million already in humanitarian need before the quakes.

nodes.label: High poverty/multidimensional poverty
nodes.description: 94% poverty rate and 46% multidimensional poverty in La Guaira; over half population in extreme poverty nationally before quakes.

nodes.label: Weak pre-existing shelter/WASH/health systems
nodes.description: REACH/ACAPS found weak shelter, water and health systems in Aragua, La Guaira, Carabobo, Falcón limiting absorptive capacity before the quakes.

nodes.label: Fragile housing stock
nodes.description: 62% of housing in fragile condition with repair needs in La Guaira; widespread housing deterioration reported pre-quake.

nodes.label: Workforce gaps from emigration
nodes.description: Years of emigration (~8 million people) left critical workforce gaps impacting search-and-rescue and recovery capacity (IRC).

nodes.label: Low Protection Cluster coverage
nodes.description: Protection Cluster had reached only 8% of its 1.9 million target population by April 2026.

nodes.label: Censorship/limited transparency
nodes.description: Censorship, limited transparency and restrictions on media/civil society weakened public trust in official information (ACAPS/Amnesty International).

nodes.label: Pre-crisis weak health system
nodes.description: Public health system in protracted collapse with shortages of personnel, medicines, supplies and surgical capacity before the quakes.

nodes.label: Need for safe temporary shelter
nodes.description: Health Cluster identified critical need for safe temporary shelter amid families sleeping in streets, cars and makeshift tents.

nodes.label: Need for safe water and sanitation
nodes.description: Water cited as top priority need nationally since March 2026; WASH gaps worsened post-quake per Health Cluster and Project HOPE.

nodes.label: Need for food and NFIs
nodes.description: Health Cluster identified critical gaps in food, hygiene kits, non-food items and clothing for affected population.

nodes.label: Need for specialized medical personnel/supplies
nodes.description: Need for logistics support, specialized medical personnel, medicines and equipment flagged by Health Cluster and PAHO.

nodes.label: Need for mental health/psychosocial support
nodes.description: Critical need for specialized MHPSS amid widespread fear, grief and distress; Project HOPE found significant MHPSS gaps.

nodes.label: Need for child protection pathways
nodes.description: Need to activate protection pathways for unaccompanied children identified in health centers.

nodes.label: Need for SRH and GBV services
nodes.description: UNFPA flagged unmet needs in survivor-centred GBV and SRH services amid overcrowded shelters and family separation.

nodes.label: Need for structural safety assessment
nodes.description: Risk that buildings not collapsed sustained unseen structural damage, requiring assessment before safe return (ACAPS).

nodes.label: Need for logistics coordination
nodes.description: OCHA Logistics Working Group identified need for coordination given congestion at airport/port, fuel shortages and access constraints.

nodes.label: Need for livelihoods/economic investment
nodes.description: IRC warned urgent investment in local economies and livelihoods is needed to prevent deepening crisis in early recovery window.

nodes.label: Need for landslide/rainfall monitoring
nodes.description: Shelter Cluster recommended daily monitoring of rainfall/landslide risk and landslide/debris-flow mapping in North Coastal Range.

nodes.label: Need for vaccine supply security
nodes.description: PAHO identified need to restore routine immunization services, cold chain and vaccine supply given outbreak risk.

nodes.label: Need for casualty registration/tracking
nodes.description: PAHO noted persistent gaps in registration and follow-up of injured/hospitalized patients causing underestimation of casualties.

nodes.label: Search and rescue operations
nodes.description: Venezuelan Red Cross and international UNDAC/USAR teams under INSARAG conducted search and rescue from 24-25 June.

nodes.label: National state of emergency declared
nodes.description: Government declared national state of emergency and designated La Guaira a disaster zone.

nodes.label: Temporary access restrictions La Guaira
nodes.description: Authorities imposed temporary access restrictions to La Guaira state from night of 26 June to prioritize search and rescue.

nodes.label: Expanded Health Cluster activation
nodes.description: Expanded Health Cluster co-led with MPPS activated 26 June to consolidate single response mechanism integrating state, UN and NGO actors.

nodes.label: IFRC DREF and Emergency Appeal
nodes.description: IFRC allocated CHF 2 million DREF and launched CHF 50-55 million Emergency Appeal targeting 300,000 people.

nodes.label: Field hospital and operations centre
nodes.description: Venezuelan Red Cross set up field hospital at Jorge García Carmeiro Stadium and a Field Operations Centre.

nodes.label: UNHCR protection and shelter support
nodes.description: UNHCR seeking $14.8-14.85M to support 30,000 people with protection, core relief items and shelter, including multi-service centres.

nodes.label: UNFPA SRH/GBV response scale-up
nodes.description: UNFPA scaling up life-saving SRH and GBV prevention/response services targeting 64,000-230,000 people.

nodes.label: UNICEF earthquake response appeal
nodes.description: UNICEF requested $65.7M to reach 470,000 people including 167,000 children, addressing health, WASH, protection and education needs.

nodes.label: NGO emergency relief mobilization
nodes.description: MSF, Good Neighbors, CESVI, Project HOPE/Proyecto Esperanza and Turkish Red Crescent mobilized relief, health posts and needs assessments.

nodes.label: OCHA Logistics Working Group services
nodes.description: LWG provides shared logistics services, transport, storage and information on access conditions, with $0.8M budget.

nodes.label: PAHO/WHO medical supply delivery
nodes.description: PAHO/WHO delivered medical supplies and equipment including to Maternal and Child Hospital Leopoldo Aguerrevere.

nodes.label: Rapid needs assessments
nodes.description: UNDAC, REACH, Project HOPE and other partners conducted rapid needs assessments of health, shelter and WASH conditions.

nodes.label: HRP Addendum and sector planning
nodes.description: OCHA Humanitarian Response Plan Addendum and UNICEF HAC Appeal Addendum outline sector plans targeting 1.3 million affected people across 7 states.

nodes.label: Health facility rehabilitation
nodes.description: Rehabilitation planning and restoration of ICU/maternity capacity at Hospital Dr. José Gregorio Hernández underway by 12 August.

nodes.label: PAHO Revolving Fund credit line
nodes.description: USD 18 million PAHO Revolving Fund credit line to support national vaccine supply security.

nodes.label: Environmental guidance for shelter response
nodes.description: Shelter Cluster/UNHCR recommended Sphere Standard 7 and ECHO Minimum Environmental Requirements for shelter siting, debris reuse and waste management.

nodes.label: Daily rainfall/landslide monitoring
nodes.description: Recommended daily monitoring of rainfall and landslide risk, plus landslide/debris-flow mapping in North Coastal Range.

nodes.label: Caribbean tsunami advisory
nodes.description: A brief Caribbean tsunami advisory was issued and cancelled within about an hour, indicating some monitoring capacity was operational.

nodes.label: Livelihoods/economic recovery investment
nodes.description: IRC recommends urgent investment in local economies and livelihood support during early recovery window.

nodes.label: Building code enforcement (lacking)
nodes.description: ACAPS notes lack of enforcement of building standards; no retrofitting or land-use planning programmes described prior to the event.

nodes.label: Venezuelan Red Cross
nodes.description: National Red Cross society conducting SAR, health posts and receiving DREF funding.

nodes.label: IFRC
nodes.description: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies supporting Venezuelan Red Cross with funding and appeals.

nodes.label: UNHCR
nodes.description: UN Refugee Agency scaling up protection and shelter response.

nodes.label: UNFPA
nodes.description: UN Population Fund scaling up SRH and GBV response.

nodes.label: UNICEF
nodes.description: UN Children's Fund providing child-focused humanitarian response.

nodes.label: PAHO/WHO
nodes.description: Pan American Health Organization/WHO co-leading Health Cluster and providing medical supplies.

nodes.label: OCHA
nodes.description: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs coordinating situation reports and logistics working group.

nodes.label: UNDP
nodes.description: UN Development Programme conducted RAPIDA damage assessment.

nodes.label: UNDRR
nodes.description: UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction produced analytical damage estimate.

nodes.label: Shelter Cluster/UNHCR
nodes.description: Shelter Cluster co-led by UNHCR issuing environmental guidance and shelter standards.

nodes.label: International NGOs (MSF, CESVI, Project HOPE, Good Neighbors, Turkish Red Crescent)
nodes.description: International NGOs providing emergency relief, health services and needs assessments.

nodes.label: IRC
nodes.description: International Rescue Committee warning on economic recovery needs.

edges.explanation: The M7.2 foreshock occurred about 39-40 seconds before the M7.5 mainshock on the same fault system.
The mainshock was followed by over 1,000 aftershocks recorded by mid-July, including notable M5.1 and M4.4 events.
Casualty figures rose steadily from the dual earthquake sequence per multiple agency sitreps.
Injury tolls rose across sitreps directly attributed to the earthquakes.
UNHCR and OCHA reported thousands of damaged/collapsed structures caused by the earthquakes.
Airport closure, metro suspension, power outages and damage to water/telecoms/roads attributed to the earthquakes.
UNDP and UNDRR estimated billions in direct physical damage from the earthquakes.
Families displaced from damaged or unsafe homes per UNHCR and UNFPA reporting.
Damaged and collapsed housing left families homeless and seeking temporary shelter.
38 hospitals reported damaged, compounding strain on an already weakened health system.
IFRC notes some missing persons figures may ultimately correspond to fatalities as registration progresses.
Damage to Maiquetía airport and concentration at Port of La Guaira increased logistics congestion risk per OCHA LWG.
Damaged WASH systems and overcrowding increase risk of vaccine-preventable and water-borne disease outbreaks per PAHO.
Ongoing aftershocks continue to weaken already damaged structures per UNHCR.
Shelter Cluster flagged increased landslide/debris-flow potential associated with seismic weakening of slopes compounded by rains.
Potential landslides/mud flows in seismically weakened slopes could further displace populations during the rainy season.
Overcrowding in shelters, family separation and displacement heightened GBV and protection risks per UNFPA.
Overcrowded temporary camps with inadequate sanitation increase risk of diarrheal and vaccine-preventable diseases per PAHO.
Extensive damage to commercial buildings and infrastructure disrupted small businesses, informal commerce and tourism per IFRC.
ACAPS/IFRC note unreinforced construction and informal hillside settlements as pre-existing risk factors that amplified structural damage.
62% of housing already in fragile condition with repair needs increased susceptibility to earthquake damage.
Pre-existing economic crisis and high inflation limit recovery capacity and amplify livelihood losses per IFRC.
High poverty (94% in La Guaira) limits households' ability to self-recover, increasing shelter needs.
REACH found weak pre-existing water, shelter and health systems in affected states limiting absorptive capacity, worsening water needs.
Pre-crisis shortages of personnel, medicines and surgical capacity compounded the health system's strain post-quake.
IRC notes mass emigration left workforce gaps that constrain search-and-rescue and recovery capacity, increasing need for economic investment.
Low pre-existing Protection Cluster coverage (8% of target) limited capacity to address heightened post-quake protection risks.
ACAPS notes censorship and limited transparency hinder situational awareness and complicate coordination, worsening registration/tracking gaps.
ACAPS reports lack of enforcement of building standards, meaning this preventive measure was absent and failed to prevent collapses.
PAHO noted persistent gaps in registration and follow-up of deaths/injuries likely causing underestimation of casualties.
Families displaced from damaged homes are staying in streets, cars and makeshift tents, generating urgent shelter needs.
Damage to water infrastructure combined with pre-existing weak systems created critical water and sanitation needs per Health Cluster.
Overwhelmed hospitals generated need for specialized medical personnel, medicines and equipment per Health Cluster.
Widespread fear, grief and distress from deaths and displacement generated critical MHPSS needs per Health Cluster.
Unaccompanied children identified in health centers required activation of protection pathways.
Heightened protection risks in overcrowded shelters drove UNFPA's identification of unmet SRH and GBV service needs.
ACAPS warns buildings that did not collapse may have unseen structural damage, requiring structural safety assessment before safe return.
Congestion at airport/port and fuel shortages generated need for logistics coordination per OCHA LWG.
Shelter Cluster identified need for daily rainfall/landslide monitoring and mapping given seismic weakening of slopes.
PAHO identified need to strengthen vaccine supply, cold chain and immunization to mitigate outbreak risk.
IRC warns loss of livelihoods and disrupted economies necessitate urgent investment to prevent deeper crisis.
Venezuelan Red Cross and international USAR/UNDAC teams conducted search and rescue to save lives after the earthquakes.
Declaration of national emergency and disaster zone designation enabled prioritized response in the hardest-hit La Guaira state.
Temporary access restrictions to La Guaira prioritized search and rescue efforts to save lives.
Expanded Health Cluster consolidated a single response mechanism integrating actors to optimize health operations on the ground.
IFRC DREF/Emergency Appeal funding targeted 300,000 people for relief including shelter support.
Field hospital at Jorge García Carmeiro Stadium added surge capacity to relieve overwhelmed hospitals.
UNHCR scaling up protection, core relief items and shelter support for 30,000 affected people.
UNHCR provides tools and equipment for identifying protection needs and facilitating referrals, including for children.
UNFPA scaling up SRH and GBV prevention/response services directly addresses identified survivor-centred service gaps.
UNICEF's $65.7M appeal addresses health, WASH, protection and education needs for 470,000 people including children.
Project HOPE and other NGOs conducted assessments and identified significant MHPSS gaps needing response.
OCHA LWG provides shared logistics services and information to address congestion and access constraints.
PAHO/WHO delivered medical supplies and equipment to hospitals including Maternal and Child Hospital Leopoldo Aguerrevere.
Rapid needs assessments by UNDAC/REACH/Project HOPE aim to consolidate evaluations and guide response, addressing data/registration gaps.
OCHA HRP Addendum and UNICEF HAC Addendum outline sector plans targeting 1.3 million affected people including recovery-oriented support.
Rehabilitation planning and restoration of ICU/maternity capacity at Hospital Dr. José Gregorio Hernández reduces ongoing health system strain.
USD 18 million PAHO Revolving Fund credit line directly supports national vaccine supply security.
Shelter Cluster recommends environmental screening, sustainable siting and daily rainfall/landslide monitoring to reduce environmental and landslide harms.
Shelter Cluster recommended daily monitoring of rainfall/landslide risk and landslide/debris-flow mapping as a preparedness measure.
A brief Caribbean tsunami advisory was issued and then cancelled, indicating functioning monitoring capacity during the event.
IRC recommends urgent investment in local economies and livelihood support during the early recovery window to prevent deepening crisis.
Venezuelan Red Cross began search-and-rescue in the Capital District on 24 June.
IFRC allocated DREF funding and launched the Emergency Appeal in support of the Venezuelan Red Cross.
Venezuelan Red Cross set up the field hospital and Field Operations Centre.
UNHCR is scaling up protection and shelter support as described in its emergency update and preparedness/response documents.
UNFPA is scaling up SRH and GBV response per its Flash Update and Country Appeal.
UNICEF's HAC Appeal Addendum requests $65.7 million for its earthquake response targeting 470,000 people.
PAHO/WHO co-leads the Expanded Health Cluster with MPPS, activated 26 June.
PAHO/WHO delivered medical supplies and equipment to affected health facilities.
PAHO's Revolving Fund credit line supports national vaccine supply security as reported in Sitrep No.9.
PAHO Sitrep No.9 reports rehabilitation planning and restoration of hospital capacity as part of early recovery efforts.
OCHA's Logistics Working Group provides shared logistics services for the earthquake response.
OCHA produced the Humanitarian Response Plan Addendum outlining sector plans for the earthquake response.
UNDP conducted the RAPIDA satellite-based rapid damage assessment within hours of the earthquake.
Shelter Cluster/UNHCR issued the Environmental Quick Note guiding the response with Sphere and ECHO standards.
Shelter Cluster recommended daily rainfall/landslide monitoring and mapping as part of its environmental guidance.
MSF, Good Neighbors, CESVI, Project HOPE and Turkish Red Crescent mobilized emergency relief and needs assessments.
IRC's 22 July statement recommends urgent investment in local economies and livelihood support.
